title: Integration of blockchain and life cycle assessment a systematic literature review
section: was carried out. Furthermore, this study extracted and synthesized the data for the themes of benefits, barriers, frameworks and models, and case studies, and conducted detailed analysis for each theme. Results and discussion The results indicated that the current state of research in this field is still in its early stages. Most articles proposed various potential benefits across different stages of the integration. However, the integration faced various technical, organizational, and system-related barriers. Only a limited number of articles presented frameworks, models, and case studies. Currently, there is a significant lack of case studies rooted in real-world data. Based on the results of the review, this study offered relevant suggestions for future development of the blockchain-LCA integration. Additionally, this study proposed a novel and practical generic framework to provide guidance for the continued advancement in this field. Conclusion This work reveals that the number of studies of blockchain-LCA integration is increasing, but this field is still in the early stages. Many potential benefits and barriers to the integration were proposed, but most of them lack validation within the existing research. In particular, there is a great need for real-world case studies. Keywords Life cycle assessment (LCA) · Life cycle inventory · Industrial ecology · Blockchain · Distributed ledger technology · Systematic review 1 Introduction Life cycle assessment (LCA) has been one of the most accepted and used tools for the estimation of potential envi- ronmental impacts for products and services around the world (Chen et al. 2014 ; Guinée et al. 2011 ; van der Giesen et al. 2020 ). It has been widely used in many fields, such as waste management, assessment and improvement of specific product systems, sustainable consumption and production, evaluation of new technologies, and promotion of proactive actions (Fröhling & Hiete 2020 ; Hellweg & Canals 2014 ). The reliability of LCA results depends on the complete- ness and accuracy of the input data. The life cycle inven- tory (LCI) analysis collects and compiles the input data for the studied product systems, which is the basis for the impact assessment of LCA (Bjørn et al. 2018 ). In prin- ciple, LCA should include the impacts of all processes over the entire lifecycle, which requires a large amount of inventory data . Ideally, an LCA study should consider all relevant input data, collect the specific primary data, and fulfill the characteristics of com- pleteness, consistency, accuracy, and transparency (Bjørn et al. 2018 ). However, in practice most studies fail to do so due to lots of reasons: (1) data collection for LCA is time-consuming and costly, and the demand for resources Communicated by D. Sica. * Lyu Zhang lyu.zhang@tum.de 1 Chair of Circular Economy, Technical University of Munich (TUM), 94315 Straubing, Germany 2 The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment (2025) 30:1-19 is too great; (2) manufacturers refuse to share information due to confidentiality; (3) the data that can be obtained is often delayed because it is usually accounted based on past operating conditions rather than current conditions; (4) the life cycle value chains are possibly very complex; (5) the geographical distribution of the supply chain is too extensive . Consequently, LCA studies usually use investigated specific data for foreground systems, and generic datasets, aggregated data, and data from litera- ture for background data, which are universal to a certain extent and could be used for a wide range of products . However, such background data are sometimes not fully representative of locally spe- cific and time-specific systems, and the lack of enough transparency leads to uncertainty and reliability concerns . Some approaches have been used to develop a variety of LCI models in order to fill the LCI data gaps, but certain challenges remain. For example, the data-driven approach faces the challenge of assessing the data quality uncertainty associated with the resulting inventory data, and the mechanistic approach requires strong discipline-specific knowledge . Besides, as an iterative method, LCA requires data transparency and traceability to enhance the credibility of the results and enable it to continuously integrate the latest data to provide more reliable information to sup- port decision-making (Björklund 2002 ). Due to the lack of a comprehensive system for the transparent collection and storage of LCI data, LCA currently lacks sufficient reliability for further application in the industry . Blockchain technology can provide an excellent solu- tion to such challenges to LCA. Blockchain is a kind of distributed ledger technology, in which all the digital events take place in a peer-to-peer network . Its main features include a decentralized database, information transparency, information invari- ance, data security, and enabling the sharing of trusted data analytics between multiple entities (Ølnes et al. 2017 ; Tang et al. 2019 ). At present, blockchain has been applied in many fields, such as financial services, insurance, healthcare, supply chain management, circular economy, and governance (Mettler 2016 ; Ølnes et al. 2017 ; Queiroz et al. 2020 ; Upadhyay et al. 2021 ). The dramatic increase in the use of RFID, sensors, and actuators and their promo- tion of automation reveal the potential of the integration of blockchain and the Internet of Things (IoT) to record, transmit, and process large amounts of data (Christidis & Devetsikiotis 2016 ; Zhang et al. 2019 ). For LCA, block- chain can bring a lot of potential benefits, such as reducing the time of LCA data collection, providing accurate and real-time inventory data, providing data transparency and traceability, and improving the credibility of LCA results (Asif & Gill 2022 ; Teh et al. 2020 ). Given such potential benefits, some works in recent years have approached integrating blockchain and LCA. Though this integration can enrich knowledge and advance the devel- opment of LCA, publications in this field only increased after 2018. Some studies analyzed the potential benefits and barriers of integrating blockchain with LCA , while some research provided a comprehensive integration framework , or conducted a case study . Karaszewski et al. ( 2021 ) summarized the trends of blockchain applying to LCA. However, there is no systematic literature review on this topic yet. Thus, a comprehensive overview of the current status, a common understanding of the topic, and research directions for the application of blockchain technology in LCA are missing. This study aims to fill the described gap. In our system- atic review, we compile all papers related to the integration of blockchain and LCA, with the objective of screening the research types and characteristics of the current papers, pro- viding an up-to-date and comprehensive state of research on blockchain-LCA integration. In doing so, we address the following research questions: - How has the scientific literature on the integration of blockchain and LCA evolved in recent years, and what is the current research status? - What themes are the current studies mainly focusing on? Which areas are covered well, and which aspects are missing? What are the potentials and limits of blockchain for LCA? - How can an integration of blockchain and LCA be achieved? What are the directions for future develop- ment? This paper proceeds as follows: Sect. 2 presents meth- ods for this systematic review; Sect. 3 shows the results, including descriptive analysis and thematic analysis; Sect. 4 discusses the current state of research on blockchain-LCA integration, provides suggestions for the future development, and proposes a new framework for the integration of block- chain and LCA in the future; and Sect. 5 presents the final conclusion. 2 Methods Referring to the PRISMA systematic review protocol , we conducted the systematic review of the current state of integration of blockchain and LCA in four steps: locating studies, study selection and evaluation, analysis and synthesis, and reporting and using the results. 3 The International Journal of Life Cycle Assessment (2025) 30:1-19 2.1 Locating studies Web of Science is the oldest, most widely used, and author- itative database of research publications and citations in the world , while SCOPUS is one of the largest curated abstract and citation databases, covering global and regional scientific publications with selected high-quality data . They have been the two most widely used databases for bibliometric analysis . Therefore, we chose Web of Science and SCOPUS to search for publications about blockchain and LCA. Two groups of expressions were used for the search: one group was for blockchain, and the other was for LCA. The first group consisted of the expressions of blockchain, block chain, and distributed ledger technology, while the second group included the expressions of life cycle assessment, life cycle analysis, and LCA. For Web of Science, the search string was (TS = (blockchain) OR TS = (block chain) OR TS = (distributed ledger technol- ogy)) AND (TS = (life cycle assessment) OR TS = (LCA) OR TS = (life cycle analysis)). For SCOPUS, the search string was (TITLE-ABS-KEY(blockchain) OR TITLE- ABS-KEY(block chain) OR TITLE-ABS-KEY(distributed ledger technology)) AND (TITLE-ABS-KEY(life cycle assessment) OR TITLE-ABS-KEY(life cycle analysis) OR TITLE-ABS-KEY(LCA)). 2.2 Study selection and evaluation Figure 1 shows the detailed steps of study selection and evaluation. We searched in June 2024 and found 210 publications in Web of Science and 456 publications in SCOPUS and managed them with EndNote. After remov- ing the duplicates, we reached 522 publications. Then we selected papers based on the inclusion and exclusion criteria: (1) peer-review journal papers were included while grey publications were excluded except conference papers since the researchers from the IT field are more inclined to publish conference papers than journal papers; (2) papers related to blockchain for LCA and blockchain- LCA integration were included, while the papers about LCA of blockchain were excluded; and (3) only papers in English were included. After removing some grey pub- lications and scanning titles, abstracts, and keywords, the set for further investigations comprised 109 papers. Next, we read the full texts of the 109 papers to conduct the content-related check and excluded those papers not related to the integration of blockchain and LCA, yielding 27 papers. Finally, we completed the snowball process for the included papers  and eventually found four related papers. As a result, a total of 31 relevant papers were identified. 2.3 Analysis and synthesis We performed the analysis and synthesis as shown in Fig. 2 . For a descriptive overview, the selected papers were exam- ined concerning the temporal, geographical, journal, and conference distribution. Besides, the industrial sectors involved in the studies about the integration of blockchain and LCA were also identified. We conducted qualitative data extraction for all the selected papers. We extracted and syn- thesized the data for the themes of benefits, barriers, frame- works and models, and case studies. We also conducted a detailed analysis of each theme. Finally, we provided our perspectives on the current research state and suggestions for future development, proposed a novel framework to pro- vide guidance for continued advancement, and presented the implications and limitations of this study. 3 Results 3.1 Descriptive analysis The descriptive analysis, in general, is characterized by the comparable small number of papers integrating blockchain and LCA, as well as their citations. As shown in Fig. 3 , the first paper on the integration of blockchain and LCA was published in 2018 due to the short history of blockchain. Three papers were published in 2018, while only one was published in 2019. After that, the number of papers on this topic increased, with eight papers in this field published in 2022. In order to provide a clear picture of the publication trend about the integration of blockchain and LCA, we compared it to the publication trends of papers on LCA and papers on blockchain. The growth rate of papers about the integration of blockchain and LCA is higher than those of these two topics. Regarding the citations, all articles have accumulated a total of 1029 citations to date, showing a consistent upward trend excluding 2024, with a peak at 303 citations in 2023. There was one paper each about leather manufacture, electronic products, and fishing and aquaculture. 3.2 Thematic analysis In order to answer the research questions, we analyzed the articles according to their thematic focus on the integration of blockchain and LCA. Specifically, four themes were iden- tified: the potential benefits, the barriers, the frameworks and models, and case studies. 3.2.1 Potential benefit There are 18 papers covering the potential benefits of the integration of blockchain and LCA. We divided these ben- efits into six groups according to the different stages of LCA: goal and scope, inventory analysis, impact assessment, inter- pretation, all the phases, and the application. The findings from the literature are explained in the following paragraphs, which are summarized in Table 1 . For the goal and scope, three papers report the potential benefits of the integration of blockchain and LCA. As the blockchain system can provide large amounts of informa- tion about the whole lifecycle of the products and services as well as the supply chains, it can provide more objective insights and reduce the need for subjective judgment, which helps to choose a more reasonable functional unit . Besides, for conducting an LCA, the scope of it is usually constrained by data availability, limited time for data collection, etc. The application of blockchain technology can improve the trace- ability and transparency of the supply chain to remove such data acquisition constraints, making it easier to define the goal and scope of LCA studies . All 18 papers mentioned the potential benefits for the inventory analysis stage. The data collection of LCA is very time-consuming and cost-intensive, while the integration of blockchain and LCA can effectively reduce the time and cost required and automatically process relevant data . Besides, it helps to improve data quality; provide more accurate, realistic, and real-time information; and reduce uncertainty . Moreover, data integrity can be ensured to account for all possible inputs in complex supply chains . This integration can ensure instant traceability and transparency of product information and data sources (Asif & Gill 2022 ; Kouhizadeh & Sarkis 2018 ). For the long-term development of LCA, it can also provide new standards for LCA data and help to establish a new transparent database . Furthermore, it can serve in the inventory analysis of specific industries, such as estimating energy consumption of transportation with the integration of GPS and assessing material regeneration and restoration effects in circular supply chains (Li & Wang 2021 ; Zhang et al. 2020 ). Seven papers provide the potential benefits for the impact assessment stage. With IoT, it can automatically calculate the environmental impacts and continuously record a large number of results under different periods and working condi- tions to form big data to explore valuable and true insights (Asif & Gill 2022 ; Karaszewski et al. 2021 ; Teh et al. 2020 ). Besides, it has the potential to provide a more fine-grained, accurate, and relevant impact assessment due to the inven- tories . The integration of blockchain and LCA can also bring benefits to the interpretation stage. It improves the accuracy and credibility of LCA results and builds consumer trust with the possibility of communicating the real-time impacts of products . In addi- tion, it has the potential to contribute to data analysis from different perspectives and provide graphical insights into LCA data . However, there is a lack of research presenting the benefits of the integration for criti- cal reviews of LCA studies. From our perspective, it makes it easier for the reviewer to validate the data quality as the blockchain can provide transparent and trackable data for the life cycle inventory analysis. Besides, it can reveal involved industries along the supply chains more transparently, which helps the organizer to find experts from related fields more appropriately for the review panel. The integration has some features that can benefit all phases of LCA. It can make it easy to prevent cheating, keep data security and privacy, and promise that enciphered private information can only be read or edited by the user who has the key . It also stores environmental information for the entire life cycle of products, helping in the management as well as recy- cling and disposal (Kouhizadeh & Sarkis 2018 ).
